sources.entry: Pomerium - Identity-aware reverse proxy, successor to now obsolete oauth_proxy. It inserts an OAuth step before proxying your request to the backend, so that you can safely expose your self-hosted websites to public Internet. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: Pomerium is an identity- and context-aware reverse proxy that gives clientless access to internal web apps and services without a corporate VPN.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Pomerium as an identity and context-aware reverse proxy that builds secure, clientless connections to internal web apps and other services. It is positioned as a way to reach internal services without a VPN, and it is deployed alongside the apps it protects rather than as a tunnel. The README says every action is verified before it is allowed to execute and that it can integrate organizational data for context-aware access decisions. The README itself gives no detailed feature list, configuration steps, or supported identity providers. Documentation and tutorials are linked externally. The awesome-selfhosted listing describes it as a successor to the obsolete oauth_proxy that inserts an OAuth step before proxying requests to a backend, so self-hosted sites can be exposed to the public Internet.
use_cases: clientless access to internal web apps without a VPN
protecting self-hosted websites behind an OAuth login
identity-aware access control for internal services
replacing a VPN for web application access
exposing self-hosted sites to the public Internet safely
notable: Clientless access to internal web apps, with no VPN or tunnel client required
Successor to the obsolete oauth_proxy, per the awesome-selfhosted listing
Every request is verified before it is allowed to execute
Context-aware access that integrates organizational data
Offers a hosted control plane and management GUI called Pomerium Zero (a paid/hosted option)
caveats: The README gives no install or configuration steps; full docs are external
Hosted control plane and management GUI are offered as a separate product, Pomerium Zero
The README states it is not a VPN alternative, despite providing VPN-free access
